doc.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: The future of jazz
summary: Hampton is optimistic that well-schooled musicians will bring jazz its rightful heritage.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: But I want to say that music is getting serious now. And you can hear some of the best jazz that you’ve ever heard now that the musicians are well prepared, they’re well schooled and they have experience, and you just can get a good insight on what they can do with their talent.
So you think the future of jazz looks pretty good?

I think so. I think jazz is going to get its rightful heritage and its home, with the talented jazz musicians we’ve got now. Because the guys are really going into the depths of music and are thinking and they’re creating and they’re doing great creations. And I think the public, if they listen, they’re in for some good rivals, you understand? Because the musicians there is are talented enough and capable enough to give them the best in jazz.
